subject.title: fix: Windows CLI backends fail through npm shims

question: Should this PR's generic Windows npm cmd-shim direct-spawn strategy be accepted for the supervisor process boundary before merge?
rationale: The code looks correct, but it changes how Windows child processes are resolved and deliberately bypasses standard npm launchers instead of using cmd.exe, which is an ownership and proof decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept after native Windows proof
options.body: Merge once a redacted Windows OpenClaw Gemini or Claude provider-launch proof link is added and required CI is green.

options.title: Accept mechanism proof now
options.body: Maintainers can merge based on the resolver tests and Node/npm contract evidence, while owning the missing final provider-launch artifact.

options.title: Pause for process-owner review
options.body: Hold the PR if generic cmd-shim bypass needs a stricter owner-approved contract or narrower rollout.

recommendation.title: Accept after native Windows proof
recommendation.body: Merge once a redacted Windows OpenClaw Gemini or Claude provider-launch proof link is added and required CI is green.

likelyOwner.reason: They are both the current PR author and the strongest feature-history owner for the Windows shim resolver and CLI backend path.
